167: function supabaseConfig() {
168:   let pageKey = null, pageUrl = null;
169:   try {
170:     const html = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'ongoing_project', 'cpp', DEFAULT_PAGE, 'index.html'), 'utf8');
171:     pageKey = (/data-supabase-anon-key="([^"]+)"/.exec(html) || [])[1] || null;
172:     pageUrl = (/data-supabase-url="([^"]+)"/.exec(html) || [])[1] || null;
173:   } catch (e) { /* no page to read; env may still carry it */ }
174: 
175:   // Read the secret from a file when one is named, so it never lands in a unit
176:   // file, in `ps`, or in `systemctl cat`. A 0600 file owned by ubuntu is a
177:   // smaller thing to get wrong than an environment variable in a committed
178:   // workflow.
179:   let fileKey = null;
180:   const keyFile = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE;
181:   if (keyFile) {
182:     try {
183:       const raw = fs.readFileSync(keyFile, 'utf8').trim();
184:       // Accept either a bare key or KEY=value, because both shapes are in the
185:       // wild and a file that silently yields '' is worse than no file at all.
186:       const m = /^\s*(?:SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(raw);
187:       fileKey = m ? m[1] : null;
188:     } catch (e) {
189:       if (process.env.SUPABASE_REQUIRE_SECRET === '1') {
190:         return { url: process.env.SUPABASE_URL || pageUrl, key: null, why: `cannot read SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE at ${keyFile}: ${e.message}` };
191:       }
192:     }
193:   }
194: 
195:   const privileged = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY || fileKey;
196:   const secret = privileged || process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY || pageKey;
197:   return {
198:     url: process.env.SUPABASE_URL || pageUrl || 'https://ltyyzxnxufvkorekglrf.supabase.co',
199:     key: secret,
200:     // What the key IS, not where it came from. A file resolving tells you
201:     // nothing about what is in it, and the publishable key resolved from a
202:     // perfectly readable 0600 file.
203:     privileged: isPrivilegedKey(privileged),
204:     keyKind: privileged
205:       ? (isPrivilegedKey(privileged) ? 'service_role' : 'not-privileged')
206:       : (isPrivilegedKey(secret) ? 'service_role' : 'publishable'),
207:   };
208: }

210: /**
211:  * Has the threading migration been applied?
212:  *
213:  * THIS EXISTS BECAUSE OF THE WORST POSSIBLE POLLER FAILURE.
214:  *
215:  * `select id from page_comments limit 1` returns `[]` both when the table is
216:  * genuinely empty and when RLS is hiding every row from this key. There is no
217:  * error, no status code, no warning. So once 20261014090000 narrows SELECT to
218:  * signed-in users, a poller still holding the publishable key reads "no /bot
219:  * comments" forever, exits 0, and stops dispatching — with nothing anywhere
220:  * saying why. The timer would look perfectly healthy.
221:  *
222:  * `parent_id` exists if and only if that migration ran, and selecting a column
223:  * that does not exist is a hard 400 rather than an empty array. That asymmetry
224:  * is the only thing that distinguishes "nothing to do" from "you cannot see
225:  * anything", and it is the only reason this function exists.
226:  */
227: async function probeThreading(cfg) {
228:   if (!cfg.key) return { threaded: false, why: 'no key' };
229:   const url = `${cfg.url}/rest/v1/page_comments?select=parent_id&limit=1`;
230:   try {
231:     const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { apikey: cfg.key, Authorization: `Bearer ${cfg.key}` } });
232:     if (res.status === 400) return { threaded: false }; // column absent -> not applied
233:     if (!res.ok) return { threaded: false, why: `HTTP ${res.status}` };
234:     return { threaded: true };
235:   } catch (e) {
236:     return { threaded: false, why: e.message };
237:   }
238: }

240: async function fetchBotComments(cfg, slug) {
241:   if (!cfg.key) return { error: 'no SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (or ANON_KEY) in the environment' };
242:   const q = new URLSearchParams({
243:     select: 'id, body, anchor, created_at',
244:     page_slug: `eq.${slug}`,
245:     order: 'created_at.desc',
246:     limit: '25',
247:   });
248:   // body is filtered by the partial index page_comments_bot_body_idx. The
249:   // supabase-js query builder cannot express `like`, so this is a raw fetch.
250:   const url = `${cfg.url}/rest/v1/page_comments?${q}&body=like.%2Fbot%25`;
251:   const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { apikey: cfg.key, Authorization: `Bearer ${cfg.key}` } });
252:   if (!res.ok) return { error: `HTTP ${res.status} — ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 160)}` };
253:   const rows = await res.json();
254:   return { rows: Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [] };

257: function bugctl(args, opts = {}) {
258:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
259:   if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'bugctl.mjs'))) {
260:     return { ok: false, why: `no bugctl at ${repo} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
261:   }
262:   const r = spawnSync('node', [path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'bugctl.mjs'), ...args],
263:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, ...opts });
264:   return { ok: r.status === 0, code: r.status, out: (r.stdout || '').trim(), err: (r.stderr || '').trim() };
265: }

267: /**
268:  * title -> { public_n, state, queue }, read once per pass.
269:  *
270:  * NOT from `bugctl create`. On the existing path create returns a stub: for a
271:  * card that was really #58 and in_fix it reported `public_n: 0`, `state: "new"`
272:  * and `queue: "ready"`, at both the top level and inside work_item. An
273:  * idempotent consumer that trusts that response re-packs a card an agent is
274:  * already working on, and `pack` overwrites the defect and resets the state —
275:  * which is exactly what un-blocks the dispatch guard for a second agent.
276:  *
277:  * So the state is read from the canonical list, once, and trusted over create.
278:  * Keyed by title because that is the only handle a page comment has: its
279:  * deterministic title_key.
280:  */
281: function bugIndex() {
282:   const r = bugctl(['list', '--json']);
283:   if (!r.ok) return { ok: false, why: r.err || `bugctl list exit ${r.code}` };
284:   let rows;
285:   try {
286:     rows = JSON.parse(r.out.slice(r.out.indexOf('{'))).rows;
287:   } catch (e) {
288:     return { ok: false, why: `could not read bugctl list: ${r.out.slice(0, 120)}` };
289:   }
290:   const map = new Map();
291:   for (const row of (rows || [])) {
292:     if (row && row.title) {
293:       map.set(row.title, {
294:         tag_id: row.tag_id || null,
295:         public_n: row.public_n || null,
296:         state: row.state || row.status || null,
297:         queue: row.queue || null,
298:       });
299:     }
300:   }
301:   return { ok: true, map };
302: }

304: /**
305:  * create -> pack -> dispatch. All three, in that order.
306:  *
307:  * `create` is idempotent by title_key, so re-running costs nothing. `pack` is the
308:  * one step that is NOT idempotent: POST /api/bugs/:id/defect overwrites item.defect
309:  * unconditionally. It is safe here only because `create` on an already-claimed
310:  * comment returns the EXISTING id and we skip straight to dispatch, whose own PID
311:  * lock refuses a second run.
312:  */
313: function fileAndDispatch(comment, parsed, slug, index) {
314:   const title = claimTitle(slug, comment.id);
315:   const known = index && index.ok ? index.map.get(title) || null : null;
316: 
317:   // THE CLAIM, and the reason this function is safe to run every five minutes.
318:   //
319:   // Read the card BEFORE creating anything. If it is already there and is past
320:   // `packed`, this comment has been dealt with: an agent is on it, or it is
321:   // awaiting verification, or it is done. Re-packing it would overwrite the
322:   // defect pack and reset the state, which is what lets the dispatch guard
323:   // admit a second agent for work already in flight.
324:   if (known) {
325:     return {
326:       stage: 'skip', ok: true, already: known.state,
327:       id: known.tag_id || null, publicN: known.public_n,
328:       why: `already ${known.state || 'filed'} — not re-filed`,
329:     };
330:   }
331: 
332:   const created = bugctl(['create', '--title', title, '--json']);
333:   if (!created.ok) return { stage: 'create', ...created };
334: 
335:   let id = null;
336:   try {
337:     const j = JSON.parse(created.out.slice(created.out.indexOf('{')));
338:     id = j.id || j.tag_id || j.public_n;
339:   } catch (e) { /* fall through to the error below */ }
340:   if (!id) return { stage: 'create', ok: false, why: `could not read an id from: ${created.out.slice(0, 160)}` };
341:   // create's own public_n is unusable (see bugIndex), so the canonical list is
342:   // asked again. One list per pass, not one per comment.
343:   const publicN = index && index.ok && index.map.get(title)
344:     ? index.map.get(title).public_n
345:     : null;
346: 
347:   const f = packFields(parsed, comment.anchor, slug);
348:   const packed = bugctl(['pack', '--id', String(id),
349:     '--component', f.component, '--observed', f.observed,
350:     '--expected', f.expected, '--criteria', f.criteria, '--json']);
351:   if (!packed.ok) return { stage: 'pack', id, ...packed };
352: 
353:   // --foreground is what makes the exit code meaningful: it says whether the
354:   // agent actually started. Under a systemd timer that is the wrong trade —
355:   // Type=oneshot stays "activating" for the whole dispatch, so the unit cannot
356:   // tick again, and a hung dispatch stops the poller entirely. --detach lets go
357:   // and takes the card + the Telegram notice as the signal instead.
358:   const dispatchArgs = [`--ticket=#${id}`];
359:   if (!has('--detach')) dispatchArgs.push('--foreground');
360:   const dispatched = spawnSync('bash',
361:     [path.join(process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'),
362:       'scripts', 'run-coding-dispatch.sh'), ...dispatchArgs],
363:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'), timeout: 900000 });
364:   const result = {
365:     stage: 'dispatch',
366:     id,
367:     publicN,
368:     ok: dispatched.status === 0,
369:     code: dispatched.status,
370:     out: (dispatched.stdout || '').trim().slice(-600),
371:     err: (dispatched.stderr || '').trim().slice(-400),
372:   };
373:   // The notice is reported, never fatal: a card that is filed and dispatched but
374:   // unsent is still filed, and failing the pass here would make the poller re-run
375:   // create/pack against a card that already exists.
376:   if (!has('--quiet-notify')) {
377:     const card = cardLabel(publicN, id);
378:   const n = notifyChat(filedNotice(card, parsed, comment, slug, result, has('--detach')));
379:     result.notified = n.ok;
380:     if (!n.ok) result.notifyWhy = n.why;
381:   }
382:   return result;
383: }

385: // ------------------------------------------------------- the notification path --
386: //
387: // WHY TELEGRAM AND NOT THE BUG API
388: // The obvious design was to POST straight to the bug store. That needs a
389: // credential off-box: bugWriteGuard accepts a token, same-origin, or loopback-only
390: // when BUG_API_TOKEN is unset — so a poller anywhere but the app box gets 401, and
391: // withFallback then QUEUES the write, returns queued:true and exits 0. A poller
392: // that cannot reach the store looks exactly like a poller that filed the work.
393: //
394: // The notification route has no such edge. Telegram is outbound-only from here:
395: // the bot's webhook (https://health-tracker.co.uk/tghook/vm) is what receives,
396: // and this site never has to accept a POST. The receiving agent already lives on
397: // the VM, where bugctl works over loopback. So no token is provisioned, nothing
398: // is provisioned, and the human sees the instruction in Telegram — which is the
399: // point of a notification rather than a silent write.
400: //
401: // WHY IT MUST BE SENT AS A USER, NOT AS THE BOT
402: // Telegram never delivers a bot's own sendMessage back to it. Sending as
403: // @VM_19485_bot would put the text in the chat and never wake the bot — it would
404: // look like it worked. scripts/lib/tg-userbot.mjs sendAsUser() is the existing
405: // user client; seat-tags.mjs uses the same session for the same reason ("a bot
406: // cannot set its own tag").
407: //
408: // sendAsUser sets no parse_mode, so none of this is Markdown: identifiers with
409: // underscores (page_comments, customer_payment) reach the bot intact. The
410: // bot-token path in telegram-send.sh hit exactly that failure and silently fell
411: // back to plain text.

413: const VM_BOT_USERNAME = 'VM_19485_bot';
414: const TG_CHAT_DEFAULT = '6218257274';

416: /** The text the VM bot receives. Self-contained: its agent has Health-tracker's
417:  *  context, not sage-prototypes', so the page, the anchor and the comment id all
418:  *  have to travel in the message. */
419: function botMessage(parsed, comment, slug) {
420:   const anchor = comment.anchor ? String(comment.anchor) : 'none (unanchored comment)';
421:   const lines = [
422:     'A /bot instruction arrived on the sage-prototypes site.',
423:     '',
424:     `repo:   /home/ubuntu/src/work/sage-prototypes`,
425:     `page:   ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}   (live: https://sage-prototypes.vercel.app/ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}/)`,
426:     `anchor: ${anchor}`,
427:     `comment id: ${comment.id}`,
428:     parsed.target ? `target agent: @${parsed.target}` : 'target agent: none named — you were chosen as the default',
429:     '',
430:     `instruction: ${parsed.instruction}`,
431:     '',
432:     'File it as a bug card (bugctl create --title "page:' + slug + ' comment:' + comment.id + '"',
433:     'then pack all four fields, then dispatch), then work it at COMPONENT level so',

475: /**
476:  * Tell the human, over Telegram, that a card exists.
477:  *
478:  * This is the part that works with nothing provisioned. telegram-send.sh already
479:  * sends as the live bot token and the delivery is verified; it needs no user
480:  * session, no teleproto and no credential off the box.

482:  * telegram-send.sh hardcodes parse_mode=Markdown and has no flag to turn it off,
483:  * so any message with two underscores fails once and retries as plain text. The
484:  * retry is invisible but the failed call is not, so Markdown-active characters
485:  * are escaped here rather than paying for a round trip every time.
486:  */
487: function escapeMd(s) {
488:   return s.replace(/([_*`[\]])/g, '\\$1');

491: function notifyChat(lines) {
492:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
493:   const sh = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'telegram-send.sh');
494:   if (!fs.existsSync(sh)) return { ok: false, why: `no telegram-send.sh at ${sh} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
495:   const text = escapeMd(String(lines).trim());
496: 
497:   // Pin the sender. Without this, telegram-send.sh falls back to ~/.hermes/.env
498:   // and every comment arrived from @Health_tracker_159bot, while deploy and push
499:   // notifications came from @VM_19485_bot — two bots, one system, and no way to
500:   // tell at a glance which notification you were looking at.
501:   //
502:   // Read from a file for the same reason as the Supabase key: `systemctl cat` and

2: // check-contrast.js — the gate that would have caught brilliant-on-grey.

10: //
11: // WHAT IT CHECKS (per component `figma/terms.json` `theme` block):
12: //   icons: every fill painted by the section's SVG assets vs the computed
13: //     stripe background, min 3.0 (WCAG 1.4.11 non-text graphics)
14: //   texts: every listed selector's computed color vs background, min 4.5
15: //     (WCAG 1.4.3 normal text; alpha is blended over the bg first)
16: // A theme change (dark<->light) must move bg + icons + text together; any
17: // one left behind fails loudly here instead of shipping quietly.
18: //
19: // USAGE
20: //   node tooling/check-contrast.js --selftest
21: //   node tooling/check-contrast.js --comp pn02-highlights-6col --url http://127.0.0.1:8901/ongoing_project/cpp/customer-payment-services/
22: // Exit: 0 pass, 1 contrast FAIL, 2 operator error, 0 + loud SKIP without Chrome.
23: 'use strict';
24: const fs = require('fs');
25: const path = require('path');
26: 
27: const ROOT = path.join(__dirname, '..');
28: const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
29: const has = f => argv.includes(f);
30: const val = (f, d) => { const i = argv.indexOf(f); return i === -1 ? d : argv[i + 1]; };
31: 
32: // ------------------------------------------------------------- pure core ---
33: function parseColor(s) {
34:   s = String(s).trim().toLowerCase();
35:   const named = { white: [255, 255, 255, 1], black: [0, 0, 0, 1] };
36:   if (named[s]) return named[s];
37:   let m = s.match(/^#([0-9a-f]{6})$/);
38:   if (m) return [parseInt(m[1].slice(0, 2), 16), parseInt(m[1].slice(2, 4), 16), parseInt(m[1].slice(4, 6), 16), 1];
39:   m = s.match(/^#([0-9a-f]{3})$/);
40:   if (m) return [0, 1, 2].map(i => parseInt(m[1][i] + m[1][i], 16)).concat(1);
41:   m = s.match(/^rgba?\(\s*([\d.]+)\s*,\s*([\d.]+)\s*,\s*([\d.]+)(?:\s*,\s*([\d.]+))?\s*\)$/);
42:   if (m) return [+m[1], +m[2], +m[3], m[4] === undefined ? 1 : +m[4]];
43:   return null;
44: }
45: function luminance([r, g, b]) {
46:   const f = c => { c /= 255; return c <= 0.03928 ? c / 12.92 : Math.pow((c + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4); };
47:   return 0.2126 * f(r) + 0.7152 * f(g) + 0.0722 * f(b);
48: }
49: // fg may carry alpha: blend over opaque bg first (how the browser paints it).
50: function ratio(fgStr, bgStr) {
51:   const fg = parseColor(fgStr), bg = parseColor(bgStr);
52:   if (!fg || !bg) return null;
53:   const a = fg[3];
54:   const eff = [0, 1, 2].map(i => fg[i] * a + bg[i] * (1 - a));
55:   const L1 = luminance(eff), L2 = luminance(bg.slice(0, 3));
56:   return (Math.max(L1, L2) + 0.05) / (Math.min(L1, L2) + 0.05);
57: }
58: // SVG asset fills: strip <defs> (clip paths paint nothing), collect fills.
59: function svgFills(text) {
60:   const noDefs = text.replace(/<defs[\s\S]*?<\/defs>/gi, '');
61:   const out = new Set();
62:   (noDefs.match(/fill\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/gi) || []).forEach(m => {
63:     const c = m.split('"')[1].toLowerCase();
64:     if (c !== 'none') out.add(c);
65:   });
66:   (noDefs.match(/style\s*=\s*"[^"]*fill\s*:\s*([^;"]+)/gi) || []).forEach(m => {
67:     const c = m.split(':').pop().trim().toLowerCase();
68:     if (c !== 'none') out.add(c);
69:   });
70:   return [...out];
71: }
72: 
73: function selftest() {
74:   let pass = 0, fail = 0;
75:   const t = (n, cond, extra) => {
76:     if (cond) pass++;
77:     else { fail++; console.log(`  FAIL ${n}${extra === undefined ? '' : ' got ' + extra}`); }
78:   };
79:   console.log('WCAG math');
80:   t('black/white is 21', Math.abs(ratio('#000000', '#ffffff') - 21) < 0.01, ratio('#000000', '#ffffff'));
81:   const jade = ratio('#008146', '#F2F5F6');
82:   t('jade on light-grey passes text bar', jade >= 4.5 && jade < 4.7, jade);
83:   const bril = ratio('#00D639', '#F2F5F6');
84:   t('brilliant on light-grey fails graphics bar', bril !== null && bril < 3.0, bril);
85:   t('identical colors are 1', Math.abs(ratio('#F2F5F6', '#f2f5f6') - 1) < 0.001);
86:   const ink = ratio('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)', 'rgb(242, 245, 246)');
87:   t('90%-black body text passes', ink !== null && ink >= 4.5, ink);
88:   t('bad color is null', ratio('nonsense', '#fff') === null);
89:   console.log('SVG fill extraction');
90:   const fills = svgFills('<svg fill="none"><defs><rect fill="white"/></defs><path fill="#008146"/><path fill="#008146"/></svg>');
91:   t('defs stripped, fills deduped', JSON.stringify(fills) === JSON.stringify(['#008146']), JSON.stringify(fills));
92:   console.log(`\n${pass} passed, ${fail} failed`);
93:   process.exit(fail ? 1 : 0);
94: }
95: 
96: // ------------------------------------------------------------------ I/O ---
97: async function run(comp, url, widths) {
98:   let puppeteer;
99:   try { puppeteer = require(path.join(ROOT, 'tooling', 'node_modules', 'puppeteer-core')); }
100:   catch { console.log('SKIP: puppeteer-core unavailable — contrast check NOT run (needs Chrome)'); process.exit(0); }
101:   const termsPath = path.join(ROOT, 'components', comp, 'figma', 'terms.json');
102:   if (!fs.existsSync(termsPath)) { console.error(`no terms.json for ${comp}`); process.exit(2); }
103:   const theme = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(termsPath, 'utf8')).theme;
104:   if (!theme) { console.error(`${comp}: terms.json has no theme block`); process.exit(2); }
105:   const exe = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome';
106:   if (!fs.existsSync(exe)) { console.log('SKIP: Chrome unavailable — contrast check NOT run'); process.exit(0); }
107: 
108:   let fails = 0;
109:   // icon assets: pure file I/O, width-independent (fail fast before Chrome)
110:   const iconColors = new Set();
111:   for (const f of (theme.icons || {}).files || []) {
112:     const fp = path.join(ROOT, theme.pageDir, f);
113:     if (!fs.existsSync(fp)) { console.log(`FAIL icon asset missing: ${f}`); fails++; continue; }
114:     svgFills(fs.readFileSync(fp, 'utf8')).forEach(c => iconColors.add(`${f}:${c}`));
115:   }
116:   if (!iconColors.size && fails === 0) { console.log('FAIL: no icon fills found'); fails++; }
117: 
118:   let browser;
119:   try {
120:     browser = await puppeteer.launch({ executablePath: exe, args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-gpu'] });
121:     const page = await browser.newPage();
122:     for (const w of widths) {
123:       await page.setViewport({ width: w, height: 900 });
124:       await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle0', timeout: 60000 });
125:       const got = await page.evaluate(sel => getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(sel)).backgroundColor, theme.bgSel).catch(() => null);
126:       if (got === null) { console.log(`FAIL ${w}: section ${theme.bgSel} missing`); fails++; continue; }
127:       console.log(`[${w}] bg ${theme.bgSel} = ${got}`);
128:       for (const ic of iconColors) {
129:         const [f, c] = ic.split(/:(?=#|\w)/);
130:         const r = ratio(c, got);
131:         const ok = r !== null && r >= (theme.icons.min || 3.0);
132:         console.log(`  ${ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'} icon ${f} ${c} vs bg = ${r === null ? 'unparseable' : r.toFixed(2)} (min ${(theme.icons.min || 3.0).toFixed(1)})`);
133:         if (!ok) fails++;
134:       }
135:       const texts = await page.evaluate(sel => {
136:         const out = {};
137:         const t = document.querySelector(sel + ' .hero-title-text-inner');
138:         const b = document.querySelector(sel + ' .score-highlight-body');
139:         if (t) out.title = getComputedStyle(t).color;
140:         if (b) { out.body = getComputedStyle(b).color; out.bodyWeight = getComputedStyle(b).fontWeight; }
141:         return out;
142:       }, theme.bgSel);
143:       for (const tx of theme.texts || []) {
144:         const key = tx.key;
145:         if (!texts[key]) { console.log(`  FAIL text ${key}: selector missing`); fails++; continue; }
146:         const r = ratio(texts[key], got);

148:         console.log(`  ${ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'} text ${key} ${texts[key]} vs bg = ${r === null ? 'unparseable' : r.toFixed(2)} (min ${(tx.min || 4.5).toFixed(1)})`);
149:         if (!ok) fails++;
150:       }
151:       if (texts.bodyWeight) console.log(`  info body fontWeight = ${texts.bodyWeight}`);
152:     }
153:   } finally { if (browser) await browser.close(); }
154:   if (fails) { console.log(`${fails} contrast failure(s) (exit 1)`); process.exit(1); }
155:   console.log('CONTRAST CLEAN');
156:   process.exit(0);
157: }

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: 'use strict';
3: /**
4:  * add-pair — create or repair an account, and keep an access code and its
5:  * auth password in step.
6:  *
7:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com            # generates a code
8:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com 24681000   # or you choose it (8+ digits)
9:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com --remove    # take access away
10:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js --list                      # who has access
11:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js --selftest                  # offline, no network
12:  *
13:  * WHY A COMMAND AND NOT AN ADMIN PAGE
14:  * Creating the Supabase account and moving its password need the service_role
15:  * key. Put that in a browser and it is in the page for anyone to read — the
16:  * service_role bypasses RLS entirely, so leaking it is leaking the table. A
17:  * command keeps the master key on one machine.
18:  *
19:  * WHERE THE PAIRS LIVE (since 2026-10-14)
20:  * public.quick_signin_accounts, verified through resolve_pair(email, code).
21:  * The admin edits rows in the comment panel (Reviewer tab -> Access) and those
22:  * edits apply immediately; nothing in this repo holds a code any more. This
23:  * tool writes the same row, plus the one thing the panel cannot do: create the
24:  * auth account or move its password.
25:  *
26:  * THE CODE IS THE ACCOUNT PASSWORD
27:  * Deliberate: the sign-in paths hand the pair straight to signInWithPassword
28:  * (or signUp on first use), so a separate secret would be a second thing to
29:  * keep in sync for no gain. resolve_pair verifies the pairing; Supabase
30:  * verifies the password.
31:  *
32:  * THE BOT ID IS WHY THE PASSWORD MOVE EXISTS
33:  * The id `bot` (typed where an email goes) signs in as bot@sage.com, a real
34:  * account, so it can comment. Changing its code in the panel changes the ROW
35:  * immediately — the gate and middleware re-resolve it — but the ACCOUNT
36:  * password is only moved here:
37:  *
38:  *   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=... node tooling/add-pair.js bot@sage.com <new code>
39:  *
40:  * on the host that holds the key. Until then the pair resolves but sign-in
41:  * refuses, which is the safe direction.
42:  */

44: const fs = require('fs');
45: 
46: const DEFAULT_URL = 'https://ltyyzxnxufvkorekglrf.supabase.co';
47: const TABLE = '/rest/v1/quick_signin_accounts';
48: const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
49: const has = f => argv.includes(f);
50: const val = (f, d) => { const i = argv.indexOf(f); return i === -1 ? d : argv[i + 1]; };
51: 
52: const isEmail = s => /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(s);
53: 
54: function makeCode() {
55:   // 10 digits from crypto, not Math.random. Readable aloud over a call, and
56:   // long enough that it is not worth guessing. (5 bytes keeps the value under
57:   // 2^53 so the modulo does not lose precision.)
58:   const c = require('crypto').randomBytes(5).readUIntBE(0, 5) % 10000000000;
59:   return String(c).padStart(10, '0');
60: }
61: 
62: // Pure paths, kept small so --selftest can cover them offline. PostgREST wants
63: // the filter value URL-encoded, or a plus-tag in an address becomes a space.
64: const listPath = () => TABLE + '?select=email,code&order=email.asc';
65: const filterPath = (email, select) => TABLE + '?'
66:   + (select ? 'select=email,code&' : '')
67:   + 'email=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(email);
68: const upsertPath = () => TABLE + '?on_conflict=email';

70: // ------------------------------------------------------------------ supabase --
71: 
72: function serviceKey() {
73:   if (process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) return process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;
74:   const f = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE;
75:   if (f && fs.existsSync(f)) {
76:     const m = /^\s*(?:SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
77:     if (m) return m[1];
78:   }
79:   return null;
80: }
81: 
82: async function api(base, key, method, path_, body, extraHeaders) {
83:   const res = await fetch(`${base}${path_}`, {

98:   return json;
99: }

101: /** Create the user, or reset the password if it already exists. */
102: async function upsertUser(base, key, email, password) {

104:   const hit = (list.users || []).find(u => (u.email || '').toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase());

124:     return;
125:   }
126:   const base = val('--url', process.env.SUPABASE_URL || DEFAULT_URL);

128:   if (has('--list')) {
129:     const rows = await api(base, key, 'GET', listPath());

131:     for (const r of rows) console.log(`    ${r.email}  code ${r.code}`);
132:     return;
133:   }
134: 
135:   const email = val('--email', argv.find(a => !a.startsWith('--')) || '');
136:   if (!email || !isEmail(email)) {
137:     console.error('  usage: node tooling/add-pair.js <email> [code] [--remove]');

139:     console.error('  needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (or SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE).');
140:     process.exitCode = 1;
141:     return;
142:   }
143:   const lower = email.toLowerCase();
144: 
145:   if (has('--remove')) {
146:     await api(base, key, 'DELETE', filterPath(lower, false));
147:     console.log(`  removed ${lower}`);
148:     console.log('  an auth account (if any) stays; with no row, resolve_pair refuses its pair.');
149:     return;
150:   }
151: 
152:   const code = val('--code', argv.find(a => /^\d{8,}$/.test(a))) || makeCode();

154:   const how = await upsertUser(base, key, lower, code);

158: }

161: 
162: function selftest() {
163:   let pass = 0, fail = 0;
164:   const t = (n, got, want) => {
165:     const a = JSON.stringify(got), b = JSON.stringify(want);

167:     else { fail++; console.log(`  FAIL  ${n}\n          got  ${a}\n          want ${b}`); }

172:     TABLE + '?select=email,code&order=email.asc');
173:   t('a filtered read selects the columns too', filterPath('a@sage.com', true),
174:     TABLE + '?select=email,code&email=eq.a%40sage.com');

179:   console.log('\ninput checking');

11: // WHERE IT RUNS

72: //
73: // MUST match components/page-comments.js parseBot. They drifted once and the
74: // panel announced one agent while the dispatcher posted to another. An `@` is
75: // required before a target, because an optional bare word is greedy: "/bot fix
76: // the second card" would parse target="fix" and eat the first word of every
77: // multi-word instruction.
78: function parseBot(body) {
79:   const text = body || '';
80:   const m = /^\s*\/bot(?:\s+@([a-z0-9_-]+))?\s+([\s\S]+)$/i.exec(text);
81:   if (!m) return null;
82:   if (!m[1] && /^\s*\/bot\s+@/i.test(text)) return null;
83:   return { target: m[1] || null, instruction: m[2].trim() };

90:  * second is refused by the store rather than by anything in this process. It must
91:  * not contain the instruction: the instruction changes if someone edits the
92:  * comment, and an edit must not become a second claim.

98: /** Pack's four fields are mandatory and the dispatcher refuses a card without

101:   const where = anchor ? anchor.replace(/^component:/, '') : 'an unanchored element';

103:     component: where,
104:     observed: `A reviewer left a comment on the ${slug} page, anchored to ${where}.`,

106:     criteria:
107:       'Make the change in the component named above only. Run node tooling/sync-check.js '
108:       + 'and node tooling/render-check.js, then commit. Report the result back on the '

114: /**
115:  * Where the poller reads from.
116:  *
117:  * The page's key is a Supabase *publishable* key — it is in the page on purpose,
118:  * and it is what the browser uses. Reading it from the same place the browser
119:  * does means a machine with the repo cloned can poll with nothing configured, and
120:  * there is no second copy of a credential to go stale.
121:  *
122:  * That only works while `page_comments` is public-read. It is not, and will not
123:  * be: 20261014090000 narrows SELECT to `auth.uid() is not null`, which is the
124:  * stated requirement — sign-in gates the panel for read AND write — and a
125:  * client-side gate is not a gate.
126:  *
127:  * So the poller needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which bypasses RLS. The publishable
128:  * key is still the default for a reason worth keeping: it is the one that works
129:  * without a secret, and probeThreading() below is what stops it being used once it
130:  * stops working. See there for why "zero rows and no error" is the most dangerous
131:  * possible outcome for a poller.
132:  *
133:  * SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE is preferred over the bare variable so the key
134:  * never appears in `systemctl cat`, `ps`, or a unit file in the repo.
135:  */
136: /**
137:  * Is this key actually privileged? A FILE RESOLVING IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION.
138:  *
139:  * This exists because the first version of the guard checked only whether
140:  * SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE had produced a string, and the publishable key
141:  * was pasted into that file by mistake. It is the same length, it is the same
142:  * value that sits in the page HTML, and the poller went green and reported "no
143:  * /bot comments" — the exact silent failure the guard was written to stop. A
144:  * guard that can be satisfied by the wrong credential is not a guard.
145:  *
146:  * So the key itself is inspected, and an unrecognised shape fails CLOSED:
147:  *
148:  *   sb_secret_…      privileged
149:  *   sb_publishable_…  NOT privileged, by definition
150:  *   eyJ…             a legacy JWT: decode the payload and read its `role`.
151:  *                     anon is not service_role, and saying so beats guessing.
152:  *   anything else    not privileged
153:  */
154: function isPrivilegedKey(k) {
155:   if (!k) return false;
156:   if (k.startsWith('sb_publishable_')) return false;
157:   if (k.startsWith('sb_secret_')) return true;
158:   if (k.startsWith('eyJ')) {
159:     try {
160:       const payload = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(k.split('.')[1], 'base64').toString('utf8'));
161:       return payload.role === 'service_role';
162:     } catch (e) { return false; }
163:   }
164:   return false;
165: }

167: function supabaseConfig() {
168:   let pageKey = null, pageUrl = null;
169:   try {
170:     const html = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'ongoing_project', 'cpp', DEFAULT_PAGE, 'index.html'), 'utf8');
171:     pageKey = (/data-supabase-anon-key="([^"]+)"/.exec(html) || [])[1] || null;
172:     pageUrl = (/data-supabase-url="([^"]+)"/.exec(html) || [])[1] || null;
173:   } catch (e) { /* no page to read; env may still carry it */ }
174: 
175:   // Read the secret from a file when one is named, so it never lands in a unit
176:   // file, in `ps`, or in `systemctl cat`. A 0600 file owned by ubuntu is a
177:   // smaller thing to get wrong than an environment variable in a committed
178:   // workflow.
179:   let fileKey = null;
180:   const keyFile = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE;
181:   if (keyFile) {
182:     try {
183:       const raw = fs.readFileSync(keyFile, 'utf8').trim();
184:       // Accept either a bare key or KEY=value, because both shapes are in the
185:       // wild and a file that silently yields '' is worse than no file at all.
186:       const m = /^\s*(?:SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(raw);
187:       fileKey = m ? m[1] : null;
188:     } catch (e) {
189:       if (process.env.SUPABASE_REQUIRE_SECRET === '1') {
190:         return { url: process.env.SUPABASE_URL || pageUrl, key: null, why: `cannot read SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE at ${keyFile}: ${e.message}` };
191:       }
192:     }
193:   }
194: 
195:   const privileged = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY || fileKey;
196:   const secret = privileged || process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY || pageKey;
197:   return {
198:     url: process.env.SUPABASE_URL || pageUrl || 'https://ltyyzxnxufvkorekglrf.supabase.co',
199:     key: secret,
200:     // What the key IS, not where it came from. A file resolving tells you
201:     // nothing about what is in it, and the publishable key resolved from a
202:     // perfectly readable 0600 file.
203:     privileged: isPrivilegedKey(privileged),
204:     keyKind: privileged
205:       ? (isPrivilegedKey(privileged) ? 'service_role' : 'not-privileged')
206:       : (isPrivilegedKey(secret) ? 'service_role' : 'publishable'),
207:   };
208: }

210: /**
211:  * Has the threading migration been applied?
212:  *
213:  * THIS EXISTS BECAUSE OF THE WORST POSSIBLE POLLER FAILURE.
214:  *
215:  * `select id from page_comments limit 1` returns `[]` both when the table is
216:  * genuinely empty and when RLS is hiding every row from this key. There is no
217:  * error, no status code, no warning. So once 20261014090000 narrows SELECT to
218:  * signed-in users, a poller still holding the publishable key reads "no /bot
219:  * comments" forever, exits 0, and stops dispatching — with nothing anywhere
220:  * saying why. The timer would look perfectly healthy.
221:  *
222:  * `parent_id` exists if and only if that migration ran, and selecting a column
223:  * that does not exist is a hard 400 rather than an empty array. That asymmetry
224:  * is the only thing that distinguishes "nothing to do" from "you cannot see
225:  * anything", and it is the only reason this function exists.
226:  */
227: async function probeThreading(cfg) {
228:   if (!cfg.key) return { threaded: false, why: 'no key' };
229:   const url = `${cfg.url}/rest/v1/page_comments?select=parent_id&limit=1`;
230:   try {
231:     const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { apikey: cfg.key, Authorization: `Bearer ${cfg.key}` } });
232:     if (res.status === 400) return { threaded: false }; // column absent -> not applied
233:     if (!res.ok) return { threaded: false, why: `HTTP ${res.status}` };
234:     return { threaded: true };
235:   } catch (e) {
236:     return { threaded: false, why: e.message };
237:   }
238: }

240: async function fetchBotComments(cfg, slug) {
241:   if (!cfg.key) return { error: 'no SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (or ANON_KEY) in the environment' };
242:   const q = new URLSearchParams({
243:     select: 'id, body, anchor, created_at',
244:     page_slug: `eq.${slug}`,
245:     order: 'created_at.desc',
246:     limit: '25',
247:   });
248:   // body is filtered by the partial index page_comments_bot_body_idx. The
249:   // supabase-js query builder cannot express `like`, so this is a raw fetch.
250:   const url = `${cfg.url}/rest/v1/page_comments?${q}&body=like.%2Fbot%25`;
251:   const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { apikey: cfg.key, Authorization: `Bearer ${cfg.key}` } });
252:   if (!res.ok) return { error: `HTTP ${res.status} — ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 160)}` };
253:   const rows = await res.json();
254:   return { rows: Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [] };

257: function bugctl(args, opts = {}) {
258:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
259:   if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'bugctl.mjs'))) {
260:     return { ok: false, why: `no bugctl at ${repo} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
261:   }
262:   const r = spawnSync('node', [path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'bugctl.mjs'), ...args],
263:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, ...opts });
264:   return { ok: r.status === 0, code: r.status, out: (r.stdout || '').trim(), err: (r.stderr || '').trim() };
265: }

267: /**
268:  * title -> { public_n, state, queue }, read once per pass.
269:  *
270:  * NOT from `bugctl create`. On the existing path create returns a stub: for a
271:  * card that was really #58 and in_fix it reported `public_n: 0`, `state: "new"`
272:  * and `queue: "ready"`, at both the top level and inside work_item. An
273:  * idempotent consumer that trusts that response re-packs a card an agent is
274:  * already working on, and `pack` overwrites the defect and resets the state —
275:  * which is exactly what un-blocks the dispatch guard for a second agent.
276:  *
277:  * So the state is read from the canonical list, once, and trusted over create.
278:  * Keyed by title because that is the only handle a page comment has: its
279:  * deterministic title_key.
280:  */
281: function bugIndex() {
282:   const r = bugctl(['list', '--json']);
283:   if (!r.ok) return { ok: false, why: r.err || `bugctl list exit ${r.code}` };
284:   let rows;
285:   try {
286:     rows = JSON.parse(r.out.slice(r.out.indexOf('{'))).rows;
287:   } catch (e) {
288:     return { ok: false, why: `could not read bugctl list: ${r.out.slice(0, 120)}` };
289:   }
290:   const map = new Map();
291:   for (const row of (rows || [])) {
292:     if (row && row.title) {
293:       map.set(row.title, {
294:         tag_id: row.tag_id || null,
295:         public_n: row.public_n || null,
296:         state: row.state || row.status || null,
297:         queue: row.queue || null,
298:       });
299:     }
300:   }
301:   return { ok: true, map };
302: }

304: /**
305:  * create -> pack -> dispatch. All three, in that order.
306:  *
307:  * `create` is idempotent by title_key, so re-running costs nothing. `pack` is the
308:  * one step that is NOT idempotent: POST /api/bugs/:id/defect overwrites item.defect
309:  * unconditionally. It is safe here only because `create` on an already-claimed
310:  * comment returns the EXISTING id and we skip straight to dispatch, whose own PID
311:  * lock refuses a second run.
312:  */
313: function fileAndDispatch(comment, parsed, slug, index) {
314:   const title = claimTitle(slug, comment.id);
315:   const known = index && index.ok ? index.map.get(title) || null : null;
316: 
317:   // THE CLAIM, and the reason this function is safe to run every five minutes.
318:   //
319:   // Read the card BEFORE creating anything. If it is already there and is past
320:   // `packed`, this comment has been dealt with: an agent is on it, or it is
321:   // awaiting verification, or it is done. Re-packing it would overwrite the
322:   // defect pack and reset the state, which is what lets the dispatch guard
323:   // admit a second agent for work already in flight.
324:   if (known) {
325:     return {
326:       stage: 'skip', ok: true, already: known.state,
327:       id: known.tag_id || null, publicN: known.public_n,
328:       why: `already ${known.state || 'filed'} — not re-filed`,
329:     };
330:   }
331: 
332:   const created = bugctl(['create', '--title', title, '--json']);
333:   if (!created.ok) return { stage: 'create', ...created };
334: 
335:   let id = null;
336:   try {
337:     const j = JSON.parse(created.out.slice(created.out.indexOf('{')));
338:     id = j.id || j.tag_id || j.public_n;
339:   } catch (e) { /* fall through to the error below */ }
340:   if (!id) return { stage: 'create', ok: false, why: `could not read an id from: ${created.out.slice(0, 160)}` };
341:   // create's own public_n is unusable (see bugIndex), so the canonical list is
342:   // asked again. One list per pass, not one per comment.
343:   const publicN = index && index.ok && index.map.get(title)
344:     ? index.map.get(title).public_n
345:     : null;
346: 
347:   const f = packFields(parsed, comment.anchor, slug);
348:   const packed = bugctl(['pack', '--id', String(id),
349:     '--component', f.component, '--observed', f.observed,
350:     '--expected', f.expected, '--criteria', f.criteria, '--json']);
351:   if (!packed.ok) return { stage: 'pack', id, ...packed };
352: 
353:   // --foreground is what makes the exit code meaningful: it says whether the
354:   // agent actually started. Under a systemd timer that is the wrong trade —
355:   // Type=oneshot stays "activating" for the whole dispatch, so the unit cannot
356:   // tick again, and a hung dispatch stops the poller entirely. --detach lets go
357:   // and takes the card + the Telegram notice as the signal instead.
358:   const dispatchArgs = [`--ticket=#${id}`];
359:   if (!has('--detach')) dispatchArgs.push('--foreground');
360:   const dispatched = spawnSync('bash',
361:     [path.join(process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'),
362:       'scripts', 'run-coding-dispatch.sh'), ...dispatchArgs],
363:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'), timeout: 900000 });
364:   const result = {
365:     stage: 'dispatch',
366:     id,
367:     publicN,
368:     ok: dispatched.status === 0,
369:     code: dispatched.status,
370:     out: (dispatched.stdout || '').trim().slice(-600),
371:     err: (dispatched.stderr || '').trim().slice(-400),
372:   };
373:   // The notice is reported, never fatal: a card that is filed and dispatched but
374:   // unsent is still filed, and failing the pass here would make the poller re-run
375:   // create/pack against a card that already exists.
376:   if (!has('--quiet-notify')) {
377:     const card = cardLabel(publicN, id);
378:   const n = notifyChat(filedNotice(card, parsed, comment, slug, result, has('--detach')));
379:     result.notified = n.ok;
380:     if (!n.ok) result.notifyWhy = n.why;
381:   }
382:   return result;
383: }

385: // ------------------------------------------------------- the notification path --
386: //
387: // WHY TELEGRAM AND NOT THE BUG API
388: // The obvious design was to POST straight to the bug store. That needs a
389: // credential off-box: bugWriteGuard accepts a token, same-origin, or loopback-only
390: // when BUG_API_TOKEN is unset — so a poller anywhere but the app box gets 401, and
391: // withFallback then QUEUES the write, returns queued:true and exits 0. A poller
392: // that cannot reach the store looks exactly like a poller that filed the work.
393: //
394: // The notification route has no such edge. Telegram is outbound-only from here:
395: // the bot's webhook (https://health-tracker.co.uk/tghook/vm) is what receives,
396: // and this site never has to accept a POST. The receiving agent already lives on
397: // the VM, where bugctl works over loopback. So no token is provisioned, nothing
398: // is provisioned, and the human sees the instruction in Telegram — which is the
399: // point of a notification rather than a silent write.
400: //
401: // WHY IT MUST BE SENT AS A USER, NOT AS THE BOT
402: // Telegram never delivers a bot's own sendMessage back to it. Sending as
403: // @VM_19485_bot would put the text in the chat and never wake the bot — it would
404: // look like it worked. scripts/lib/tg-userbot.mjs sendAsUser() is the existing
405: // user client; seat-tags.mjs uses the same session for the same reason ("a bot
406: // cannot set its own tag").
407: //
408: // sendAsUser sets no parse_mode, so none of this is Markdown: identifiers with
409: // underscores (page_comments, customer_payment) reach the bot intact. The
410: // bot-token path in telegram-send.sh hit exactly that failure and silently fell
411: // back to plain text.

413: const VM_BOT_USERNAME = 'VM_19485_bot';
414: const TG_CHAT_DEFAULT = '6218257274';

416: /** The text the VM bot receives. Self-contained: its agent has Health-tracker's
417:  *  context, not sage-prototypes', so the page, the anchor and the comment id all
418:  *  have to travel in the message. */
419: function botMessage(parsed, comment, slug) {
420:   const anchor = comment.anchor ? String(comment.anchor) : 'none (unanchored comment)';
421:   const lines = [
422:     'A /bot instruction arrived on the sage-prototypes site.',
423:     '',
424:     `repo:   /home/ubuntu/src/work/sage-prototypes`,
425:     `page:   ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}   (live: https://sage-prototypes.vercel.app/ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}/)`,
426:     `anchor: ${anchor}`,
427:     `comment id: ${comment.id}`,
428:     parsed.target ? `target agent: @${parsed.target}` : 'target agent: none named — you were chosen as the default',
429:     '',
430:     `instruction: ${parsed.instruction}`,
431:     '',
432:     'File it as a bug card (bugctl create --title "page:' + slug + ' comment:' + comment.id + '"',
433:     'then pack all four fields, then dispatch), then work it at COMPONENT level so',
434:     'future instances inherit the fix. Do not patch the page fragment.',

476:  * Tell the human, over Telegram, that a card exists.
477:  *
478:  * This is the part that works with nothing provisioned. telegram-send.sh already
479:  * sends as the live bot token and the delivery is verified; it needs no user
480:  * session, no teleproto and no credential off the box.
481:  *
482:  * telegram-send.sh hardcodes parse_mode=Markdown and has no flag to turn it off,
483:  * so any message with two underscores fails once and retries as plain text. The
484:  * retry is invisible but the failed call is not, so Markdown-active characters
485:  * are escaped here rather than paying for a round trip every time.
486:  */
487: function escapeMd(s) {
488:   return s.replace(/([_*`[\]])/g, '\\$1');

491: function notifyChat(lines) {
492:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
493:   const sh = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'telegram-send.sh');
494:   if (!fs.existsSync(sh)) return { ok: false, why: `no telegram-send.sh at ${sh} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
495:   const text = escapeMd(String(lines).trim());
496: 
497:   // Pin the sender. Without this, telegram-send.sh falls back to ~/.hermes/.env
498:   // and every comment arrived from @Health_tracker_159bot, while deploy and push
499:   // notifications came from @VM_19485_bot — two bots, one system, and no way to
500:   // tell at a glance which notification you were looking at.
501:   //
502:   // Read from a file for the same reason as the Supabase key: `systemctl cat` and
503:   // `ps` are world-readable, so the token belongs in a 0600 file rather than in
504:   // the unit or in the repository.
505:   const env = Object.assign({}, process.env);
506:   if (!env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) {
507:     const f = process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_FILE;
508:     if (f && fs.existsSync(f)) {
509:       const m = /^\s*(?:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
510:       if (m) env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN = m[1];
511:     }
512:   }
513: 
514:   const r = spawnSync('bash', [sh, `--text=${text}`],
515:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, env });
516:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
517:   return {
518:     ok: r.status === 0,
519:     out: out.slice(-160),
520:     why: r.status === 0 ? null
521:       : ((r.stderr || '') + ' ' + out).trim().split('\n').pop().slice(0, 160),
522:   };
523: }

783:       console.error('    The publishable key now reads ZERO rows with NO error, so a poll here');
784:       console.error('    would report "no /bot comments" forever while dispatching nothing.');
785:       console.error('    Fix: set SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE to a 0600 file holding the');
786:       console.error('    project SECRET key (Dashboard -> Project Settings -> API Keys -> the');
787:       console.error('    sb_secret_ one, NOT the sb_publishable_ one shown beside it).');
788:       process.exitCode = 1;
789:       return;
790:     }
791:     console.log(`  using the ${cfg.keyKind} key — threading is not applied yet, so reads are still open`);
792:   }

795:   if (got.error) { console.error(`  cannot read comments: ${got.error}`); process.exitCode = 1; return; }
796:   if (!got.rows.length) { console.log('  no /bot comments'); return; }
797:   console.log(`  ${got.rows.length} /bot comment(s)`);

799:   const notify = has('--notify');
800:   // One canonical read of the store per pass, so a comment already dealt with is
801:   // recognised as such instead of being re-packed and re-dispatched every tick.
802:   let index = { ok: false, map: new Map() };

804:     index = bugIndex();

811:     const r = notify ? notifyVmBot(parsed, c, slug) : fileAndDispatch(c, parsed, slug, index);
812:     if (!r.ok) anyFail = true;

818:     // is about, introduced by the fix for it.
819:     const sent = r.notified === false ? 'NOT SENT — ' + (r.notifyWhy || 'unknown') : (r.to ? ' → ' + r.to : '');

821:       + (r.ok
